course_name_original: Programmable Electronics and Digital Signal Processing
course_name_en: Programmable Electronics and Digital Signal Processing

learning_outcomes.text: Understand, design and implement digital signal analysis in the time domain and frequency domain using data acquisition platforms and real-time platforms with DSP.
Understand how digital filters work and carry out the design and implementation of digital filters.
Understand and know how to use programming languages and software tools associated with digital signal processing.
Develop digital signal processing systems based on basic I/O platforms and real-time platforms with DSP.

syllabus_topics: Analog and digital signals, real-time platforms stop digital signal processing, advantages and disadvantages of signal processing
Digital analog conversion: Sampling, quantization and coding
Analog Digital and Digital Analog Converters
Hardware and Software for digital signal processing systems: MyDAQ, MyDSP LabVIEW Programming
Digital filters: filters with finite (FIR) and infinite (IIR) impulsive response - design and implementation
Digital signal processing applications: audio processing, spectral analysis

assessment_methods.method: Examination (1st sitting, 2nd sitting, and special examination sitting)

assessment_rules: For assessment throughout the semester, students must achieve a minimum mark of 8 for each laboratory report and 8 for the test. The course can also be assessed 100% by examination. Attendance at laboratory sessions counts for 100% of the examination-based assessment, while attendance at theory sessions or theory and practical sessions counts for 50%. Should objective reasons for absence from laboratory sessions be recorded, arrangements will be made with the lecturer to make up for the missed sessions.
